scope: Original exposed corpus ticket-triage workload on Azure. The same22 provider-neutral criteria and three natural follow-ups are frozen before generation; only the explicitly requested target provider changes from the earlier AWS map. No SDK, architecture, resource addresses or expected answer is prescribed. Evaluator-authored, not blinded holdout.
clarifications: Ten staff and daily usage are planning inputs, not invented hard licensing/concurrency/customer quotas.
Synthetic/redacted input is supplied by the client; automatic redaction was not requested.
20 KB has a unit convention ambiguity: assess documented convention, support for 20,000 UTF-8 bytes and a finite upper bound, rather than silently inventing a new business decision.
Local/cloud-vendor emulation is permitted by the owner. Actual cloud deployment and authenticated cloud-account calls are not required or authorized.
A missing, skipped or unexecuted critical check is not a pass; no complete-project count is awarded for component or generated-test coverage.

checks.requirement: Microsoft Azure is retained as the target provider; the model backend is not confused with the target cloud.
Implement an internal staff-facing pasted-ticket review tool, including usable browser/API/application artifacts.
Return summary, topic, suggested urgency and uncertainty through a documented validated JSON contract.
Suggestions remain subject to human review, with a visible review-only notice and no automatic customer action.
Do not connect to or modify the existing help desk or customer records; preserve its ownership boundary.
Only authorized signed-in staff may submit tickets; denied and malformed identities fail closed.
The design and operating/cost assumptions account for ten staff and about 200 tickets per working day without inventing a customer quota or SLA.
Five simultaneous valid requests complete safely without cross-request data or identity leakage.
Support synthetic/redacted pasted ticket text up to the stated 20 KB, with a declared Unicode byte/character/unit convention and an enforced bound.
Reject missing, malformed, wrong-type and oversized input without returning a fabricated suggestion or unsafe diagnostic.
Raw ticket text is not written to persistent browser/server/object/database/log storage after processing; retention limits are explained precisely.
Processing uses an Australian region supported by selected services; any global/foreign/unknown paths are explicitly flagged and no silent regional fallback occurs.
Provide a modest justified starting footprint and sourced costs or explicit unknown rates; do not invent prices, currency, monthly workdays or model usage as facts.
Model timeout, refusal, malformed/truncated output and provider denial produce safe failure and allow subsequent recovery without hidden retries or customer writes.
The reviewer can clear a displayed suggestion and sees uncertainty explicitly; stale concurrent/cancelled responses do not restore cleared content.
Emitted infrastructure initializes offline, formats and validates against its real pinned provider schema; connections and identities are concrete.
Application configuration, identity/scopes, resources/permissions, model endpoint and browser/API interfaces agree; mock tests do not substitute for independent connection checks.
A clean unpack builds/tests the actual implementation using documented/pinned dependencies and target runtime; generated test success is independently checked.
Simple build/run/maintenance/failure/recovery/rollback instructions identify required operator inputs and account/model unknowns.
No real credentials or private keys are embedded or requested by the local evaluation; only explicit synthetic fixtures are used.
Retain all ordered client follow-ups and exact model/effort; material questions are distinguished from routine technical choices.
Exercise an independent browser-to-application success/denial/input/model-failure/recovery/clear journey against local service/identity/model contracts, labeling emulated vendor behavior.
